newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ABERDEEN SHARE POINTS IN SIX-GOAL THRILLER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ABERDEEN SHARE POINTS IN SIX-GOAL THRILLER.

text.p: Aberdeen, seeking to close the gap on Rangers and Celtic, were forced to share the points in a six-goal thriller with Dundee United in the Scottish premier division on Saturday.
The two top clubs played in midweek, with Rangers winning 1-0 to take a three- point lead over Celtic.
Aberdeen went in front after 25 minutes, Bulgarian Ilian Kiriakov scoring his first goal since signing for the club.
Dundeed equalised on the stroke of half-time when Andy McLaren turned in a cross by Kgell Olufsson.
The second half provided pulsating end-to-end action, with Erik Pederson picking out Robbie Winters with a long diagnonal pass for the youngster to race in and give the visitors the lead.
French stopper Toni Kombouare struck Aberdeen's equaliser with a glancing header from a corner with just 12 minutes left.
Olufsson re-established the visitors' initiative two minutes later with a terrific finish from a McLaren cross but Aberdeen refused to give in.
Billy Dodds ensured they shared the spoils with a spectacular diving header two minutes from time for his 18th of the season.

Hearts stayed level with Aberdeen on 19 points, 10 behind Rangers, when they were held to a goalless draw at home by Hibernian who were reduced to 10 men shortly after the interval when John Hughes was sent off.
Hughes had been booked in the first half after what looked an innocuous challenge on Stephane Paille.
Five minutes after the re-start Hughes appeared to make contact with Paille using his arm. The Frenchman made the most of the challenge and Hughes was sent off.
Goalkeeper Jim Leighton was booked in the aftermath for dissent and became the target for coins from a minority of Hearts fans.
